_meta.description: Eight cross-disciplinary knowledge domains available to all agents. Each domain contains analytics translations — how the discipline's methods apply to the Financial Impact Analysis context.

disciplines.name: Advanced Mathematics
analytics_translations: Optimization of metric definitions under multi-objective constraints (e.g., precision/recall Pareto front for fraud detection thresholds)
Convex relaxations for experiment design problems (sample size optimization under budget constraints)
Topological data analysis for detecting structural changes in abuse pattern shape
Information geometry for comparing probability distributions in data quality monitoring

disciplines.name: Physics (First Principles)
analytics_translations: Conservation laws applied to data flow: events_in = events_recorded + losses + sampling_error — use to detect silent data loss
Entropy production rate as a data-quality scalar: high entropy = structural breakdown, not just noise
Percolation theory for cluster growth and phase transitions in abuse networks
Thermodynamic equilibrium framing: abuse detection as a system trying to return to low-entropy state

disciplines.name: Computational Theory
analytics_translations: Hardness bounds on what analytical questions are tractable at scale (NP-hardness of exact cluster enumeration)
Complexity analysis of pipeline designs (time complexity of each transformation step)
Approximation algorithm selection for graph-analysis tasks (spectral clustering vs. exact partitioning)
Information-theoretic bounds on detection: minimum description length of coordinated abuse signal

disciplines.name: Programming Logic
analytics_translations: Type-theoretic metric specifications — metrics as formal types, query generation as type-checking
Formal verification of pipeline correctness (dbt test suites as executable specifications)
Dependent types for artifact schemas (artifact_type determines which fields are required)
Logic programming for constraint propagation in governance rule enforcement

disciplines.name: Network Science
analytics_translations: Graph motif detection for coordinated abuse cluster topology (star, chain, bipartite core-periphery)
Percolation threshold monitoring on account connectivity graphs
PageRank-style centrality for identifying orchestrators within abuse clusters
Community detection algorithms (Louvain, spectral) for cluster identification
Temporal graph analysis: edge appearance timing correlates with coordinated behavior

disciplines.name: Game Theory
analytics_translations: Stackelberg framing for metric design: if we publish this KPI, what behavior does it incentivize at equilibrium?
Mechanism design for fraud detection thresholds: set thresholds to minimize total exploitation, not just catch detected violators
Adversarial game trees for experiment design: model how malicious actors would optimize against the proposed detection system
Nash equilibria in abuse/detection arms race: characterize long-run behavior

disciplines.name: Cryptography
analytics_translations: Commitment schemes for pre-registered experiment hypotheses (prevent p-hacking post-hoc)
Zero-knowledge attestations for data access patterns (prove a query was valid without revealing query content)
Hash-chaining for artifact immutability verification
Secure computation for multi-party metric computation (Phase 7+)

disciplines.name: Historical Precedent
analytics_translations: Defense-in-depth applied to data pipeline architecture: multiple independent quality checks, not a single gate
Least-privilege access model: agents have bounded toolsets, not general-purpose access
Fail-secure defaults: when in doubt, gate for human review rather than auto-approve
Post-mortem culture: every pipeline failure produces a documented postmortem with root-cause, remediation, prevention triad
Red-teaming as standard pre-shipment practice (analogous to pre-production code review)
